children: Honeywell Aerospace

announced two developments spanning its commercial aviation aftermarket and defense businesses, including a maintenance agreement with Garuda Indonesia and a cooling-system upgrade for the F-35 fighter.
Garuda signs three-year APU agreement
Honeywell Aerospace
signed a three-year agreement with PT Garuda Indonesia to provide repair and maintenance services for auxiliary power units across the airline's fleet.

The agreement covers Honeywell's 131-9B, 331-350 and 331-500 APU models. It establishes a multi-year framework intended to give Garuda more predictable repair costs and service expectations as it plans aircraft maintenance.
APUs provide electrical power and conditioned air while aircraft are on the ground, including during boarding and turnaround. Honeywell Aerospace
operates 26 repair and overhaul facilities globally and works with more than 100 commercial air transport channel partner locations.
The agreement expands Honeywell Aerospace's
aftermarket business in Indonesia and the broader Asia-Pacific region. Financial terms weren't disclosed.
F-35 cooling capacity gets a boost
Separately, Honeywell Aerospace
launched an upgrade to the Power and Thermal Management System used on the F-35 fighter aircraft.
The P40 upgrade is designed to increase cooling capacity by 25%, from about 32 kilowatts to 40 kilowatts. Honeywell Aerospace
said the upgrade relies on software changes and targeted liquid-cooling improvements and doesn't require modifications to the aircraft's airframe.

The company expects the technology to be fielded between 2029 and 2030. It can be incorporated alongside the F-35's planned Engine Core Upgrade, allowing the work to take place during scheduled maintenance.
Honeywell Aerospace

said corrective actions incorporated into P40 are projected to reduce Honeywell-attributable non-resettable in-flight shutdowns by about 30%. The company's existing PTMS has accumulated more than 1 million flight hours across the global F-35 fleet.
The architecture also provides a path to increase cooling capacity eventually to 62 kilowatts or more as the F-35 adds more power-intensive sensors, electronics and processing capabilities.
